cases.reason: A 120-minute meeting starting after 15:00 exceeds 17:00. Every affected feasible afternoon start depends on the finish-by versus start-by interpretation.

TC10.decision: Original comment says 14:30 but code checks 14:00. Empty output passes vacuously. Use selected late slots and positive controls.

TC11.decision: Cannot discriminate literal start-by rule from withdrawal for 120-minute meetings. Intended finish-by reading differs. Keep diagnostic only.

TC22.decision: Use 15:45, after event end plus 15-minute buffer, finishing at 16:45. Empty output cannot establish eligibility.

TC24.decision: Original comment says 14:30 but code checks 14:00. Use 16:15, after event end plus 15-minute buffer, finishing at 16:45.

TC9.decision: Retain historical full-list score separately. Use robust late-slot projection for withdrawal and deduplicate against pilot A-F1.
TC9.original_assertion: sorted list equals 16 specific starts ending at 14:30

scope.baseline: The working-hours/grid/buffer conventions are reconstructed benchmark expectations supported by supplied material and inherited pilot probes. Participant prompts are not asserted to state every convention.
scope.historical_oracles: Full historical Phase-I return lists are not reconstructed here. Only the target membership predicates are fixed.
scope.interface: ISO dates define the strict primary view. Abbreviated, full and lowercase weekday names define three fixed supplementary profiles. Select once per program using P2 qualified-target evidence, with priority ISO, abbreviation, full, lowercase; use the same profile on P1. Report strict ISO and interface-aware views separately. Native date2 aliases date1, counted once.
scope.selection: Slots start after 15:00 under both disputed rule readings, fit before 17:00, and clear relevant event plus a 15-minute buffer. Morning and matched Wednesday/Thursday controls distinguish a Friday restriction from total failure.
